clue.text: His work can be a bit of a trial

definitions.text: His work can be a bit of a trial

parts.words: His work can be a bit of a trial
parts.note: a writer whose best-known novel is The Trial, about Josef K's baffling prosecution, so his work is literally a trial

explanation.surface: A grumble that some author's books are hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech author of The Trial and The Castle, whose prose is notoriously demanding.

clue.text: Piece inspired by "the milk of paradise"

definitions.text: Piece inspired by "the milk of paradise"

parts.words: Piece inspired by "the milk of paradise"
parts.note: the Coleridge poem that ends with 'drunk the milk of Paradise', itself said to have come from an opium dream

explanation.surface: A work of art said to have been prompted by some heavenly drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's opium-dream poem closes with the line about having drunk the milk of Paradise.

clue.text: Subtle assistant's?

parts.note: in Jonson's The Alchemist the trickster Subtle is helped by a servant called Face, master of many disguises

explanation.surface: Asking what belongs to a discreet helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' looks like an adjective, but it is the alchemist in Ben Jonson's comedy; his accomplice wears many masks, so the plural fits too.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonson's con man Subtle relies on a sidekick named Face, who puts on one disguise after another.

clue.text: Club review

definitions.meaning: a famous gentlemen's club on Pall Mall in London
a Victorian literary and critical journal of the same name

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Pall Mall gentlemen's club and a celebrated nineteenth-century literary weekly bear this classical name.

clue.text: Moore rank revised by Fleming

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Roger Moore's billing reconsidered by a producer called Fleming.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Moore starred in the film of this Bond novel, so the surface is apt; 'by Fleming' defines it as a work by Ian Fleming.
explanation.definitionFit: A James Bond novel written by Ian Fleming in 1955.

clue.text: This wartime heroine is, er, mine

definitions.text: This wartime heroine is, er, mine

parts.words: This wartime heroine is, er, mine
parts.note: Jan Struther's Mrs ___, the Second World War heroine of book and film; said quickly her title sounds like 'missus mine, ever'

explanation.surface: Someone claiming, a little hesitantly, to own a war heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Miniver is the British housewife heroine of Jan Struther's sketches and the 1942 Greer Garson film.

clue.text: Lady Nicolson inspired him, er, her

definitions.text: Lady Nicolson inspired him, er, her

parts.words: Lady Nicolson inspired him, er, her
parts.note: Vita Sackville-West, wife of Harold Nicolson, was the model for Virginia Woolf's hero who changes sex midway through the novel

explanation.surface: A muddled remark about whom a titled lady inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Nicolson is Vita Sackville-West; the stumble 'him, er, her' reflects the Woolf character turning from man to woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's 1928 novel hero, modelled on Vita Sackville-West, lives for centuries and becomes a woman.

clue.text: Golding ceremonial confined to lobby?

parts.note: A lobby is a passage, so ceremonies of a passage

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a gilding ritual is kept to the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonies or rituals, as in the title of Golding's Booker-winning Rites of Passage.

clue.text: Shrew recalled by Anya Seton?

definitions.meaning: Kate, the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, has this full name
Anya Seton's historical novel about ... Swynford, John of Gaunt's mistress, bears this title

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tamed shrew and the title of Anya Seton's 1954 historical novel share this female name.

clue.text: Regretting decline of the guinea

parts.note: decline as a noun means ruin or downfall
G is an abbreviation for guinea, an old British coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: Lamenting how an old gold coin lost its value.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow or remorse over something, a synonym.

clue.text: A Bach clan composed for revelry

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A family of Bachs wrote music for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken celebration or orgy, named after Bacchus, god of wine.

clue.text: All-italian part of John Byrne story

definitions.text: All-italian part of John Byrne story

parts.words: All-italian part of John Byrne story
parts.note: Its first word is Italian for 'all', a musical term

explanation.surface: A section of a Scottish writer's tale described as entirely Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for all, used in music for the whole ensemble, and half the title of Byrne's Tutti Frutti.

clue.text: Indians once consumed English voyager

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up within these words, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A tale of an English explorer eaten by Native Americans long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: George, Lord Anson, the English admiral who sailed round the world in the 1740s.

clue.text: "Here is … situated the grotto … into which she enticed Tannhäuser; fine view from the top." (Baedeker, via Anthony Powell)

definitions.text: "Here is … situated the grotto … into which she enticed Tannhäuser; fine view from the top." (Baedeker, via Anthony Powell)

parts.words: "Here is … situated the grotto … into which she enticed Tannhäuser; fine view from the top." (Baedeker, via Anthony Powell)
parts.note: the goddess of love lured Tannhauser into her mountain grotto in German legend and Wagner's opera; Powell borrowed the name for his first novel's title

explanation.surface: A guidebook entry, quoted by a novelist, about a legendary grotto with a view.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain of the love goddess in the Tannhauser legend, also the title of Anthony Powell's 1933 novel.

clue.text: Arrogance of hot French film director

parts.note: H stands for hot, as on a tap
auteur is the French term for a film director with a strong personal style

explanation.surface: A temperamental filmmaker from France is accused of arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughtiness or lofty pride, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We ruined a compostion, yet not tired

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: We spoiled a piece of music but are still full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compostion' is printed so, a slip for composition; it still signals the anagram of WE RUINED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining fresh and untiring, never fatigued.

clue.text: Theatre presenting me in musical based on Dickens

indicators.note: in places the word for me inside the musical's title

parts.note: Lionel Bart's musical Oliver! adapts Oliver Twist
I is the speaker's own word for me

explanation.surface: A playhouse staging me in Bart's Dickens show.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest auditorium of London's National Theatre, named after Laurence Olivier.

clue.text: Youthful situation of he who observed "the past is a foreign country"

annotationWithheld.why: Youthful situation of he who observed "the past is a foreign country" (2,7): the clue points to Hartley's The Go-Between (GO-BETWEEN), but the answer is held as IN BETWEEN; no crossing data to confirm which.
annotationWithheld.clue: Youthful situation of he who observed "the past is a foreign country"

clue.text: River animal and mother in port

parts.note: the otter is a riverside animal
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A river creature and its mother found in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Dutch port city on the Maas delta.

clue.text: Chap follows directions on paper

indicators.note: follows puts the word for chap after the directions

parts.note: north, east, west and south give N, E, W and S
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow obeys instructions written down.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist working for a newspaper is on the paper.

clue.text: Disastrously tempting production of Charlotte Haze

definitions.text: Disastrously tempting production of Charlotte Haze

parts.words: Disastrously tempting production of Charlotte Haze
parts.note: in Nabokov's Lolita, Charlotte Haze's daughter is the girl Humbert finds fatally alluring

explanation.surface: A warning about an alluring but ruinous show starring one Charlotte Haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's coinage for a sexually precocious young girl, applied to Lolita, Charlotte Haze's child.

clue.text: Index of titles, so to speak

definitions.text: Index of titles, so to speak

parts.words: Index of titles, so to speak
parts.note: the reference work listing the peerage and baronetage, a catalogue of noble titles rather than book titles

explanation.surface: Something like a list of book names.
explanation.definitionFit: Debrett's Peerage, the standard guide to British aristocracy and their titles.

clue.text: Frequent visitor to the fair (not always to see Fifine)

definitions.text: Frequent visitor to the fair (not always to see Fifine)

parts.words: Frequent visitor to the fair (not always to see Fifine)
parts.note: the fair means fair women; in Browning's Fifine at the Fair the speaker is the legendary seducer

explanation.surface: Someone who goes to the funfair often, not always for one performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seducer, a womaniser who pursues the fair sex, and the speaker of Browning's poem.

clue.text: The —("Perhaps the finest Western in the history of the film", according to Greene)

definitions.text: The —("Perhaps the finest Western in the history of the film", according to Greene)

parts.words: The —("Perhaps the finest Western in the history of the film", according to Greene)
parts.note: the 1936 Cecil B DeMille Western starring Gary Cooper, praised by Graham Greene as a film critic

explanation.surface: Graham Greene's praise of a Western, with its title left blank.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontiersman of the prairies; The ___ is the 1936 Gary Cooper Western Greene admired.

clue.text: She revealed a connection between Worthing and Brighton

definitions.text: She revealed a connection between Worthing and Brighton

parts.words: She revealed a connection between Worthing and Brighton
parts.note: in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest the governess confesses she left baby Jack Worthing in a handbag at Victoria, on the Brighton line

explanation.surface: A woman uncovering a link between two Sussex seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Worthing and Brighton look like neighbouring south-coast towns; Worthing is Wilde's hero, found on the Brighton line.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Prism, the absent-minded governess whose handbag mix-up launches Wilde's plot.

clue.text: Alan Paton's birthplace was like everyone else's …

definitions.text: Alan Paton's birthplace was like everyone else's …

parts.words: Alan Paton's birthplace was like everyone else's …
parts.note: Paton was born in a South African province of this name, and every birthplace is related to birth

explanation.surface: Remarking that a famous author's birthplace was quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to birth, and the former South African province where Paton was born.

clue.text: It is not your trade to make-s—" (S. Johnson)

definitions.text: It is not your trade to make-s—" (S. Johnson)

parts.words: It is not your trade to make-s—" (S. Johnson)
parts.note: Johnson said a critic may scold a carpenter for bad furniture without being able to make it himself

explanation.surface: A Johnson quotation with its key word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of furniture that a carpenter, not a critic, builds, in Boswell's report of Johnson.

clue.text: He arranged notes concerning Israel and America

definitions.text: He arranged notes concerning Israel and America

parts.words: He arranged notes concerning Israel and America
parts.note: the Swiss-American composer wrote an Israel Symphony and the epic rhapsody America

explanation.surface: A diplomat who drafted memoranda about two allied nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Bloch, Swiss-born composer of Schelomo, the Israel Symphony and America.

clue.text: Wordsworth's boy reaches maturity in Dostoevsky?

definitions.text: Wordsworth's boy reaches maturity in Dostoevsky?

parts.words: Wordsworth's boy reaches maturity in Dostoevsky?
parts.note: Wordsworth wrote The ___ Boy; Dostoevsky's novel The ___ is about the grown-up Prince Myshkin

explanation.surface: A poet's child character growing up inside a Russian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or simpleton, title word of Wordsworth's ballad and Dostoevsky's novel.

clue.text: Domestic novelist?

definitions.meaning: relating to the home and family
Geoffrey ___, author of the thriller Rogue Male

explanation.definitionFit: Means belonging to the home, and is the surname of thriller writer Geoffrey of Rogue Male.

clue.text: Average weight of The Changeling author

parts.note: middle means average or medium
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A medium-weight writer of a Jacobean tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Middleton co-wrote the Jacobean tragedy The Changeling with William Rowley.

clue.text: Some profit, we hear, derived from China, humble though it be

indicators.note: derived from means taken out of these words, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A modest gain made from porcelain, however small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profit, we hear' sounds like prophet: this is a minor Old Testament prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor prophet of the Old Testament whose book foretells Nineveh's fall.
